Own HR Operations for North America across the employee lifecycle, while partnering on selected global processes and initiatives.

Significant policy design and transition (ex: you made a large scale global policy change and drove the change management)

Job Description Summary

The Human Resources Business Partner is an individual contributor who combines hands-on execution with proactive partnership across assigned client groups. Reporting to a Senior HR Business Partner, this role serves as a trusted advisor to managers and leaders, translating business priorities and workforce needs into practical people strategies and solutions. The HRBP operates with meaningful autonomy, builds strong relationships with stakeholders, coaches managers through a broad range of people matters, and uses data and business context to identify trends, anticipate needs, and recommend action. The ideal candidate is comfortable navigating ambiguity, managing competing priorities, and knowing when to independently resolve an issue versus partnering with or escalating to the Senior HRBP, Employee Relations, Legal, or other People teams.

This role will support assigned client groups within Sales, Marketing, Product, and/or other business functions in a collaborative, matrixed, remote-first environment. The HRBP will independently own day-to-day HR partnership within a defined scope while providing visibility, recommendations, and escalation on complex or high-impact matters to the Senior HRBP.

Essential Responsibilities

Provide independent, day-to-day HR partnership to assigned managers and employees, serving as a trusted resource for practical guidance and solutions.
Build a strong understanding of assigned client groups’ business priorities, workforce needs, organizational context, and culture to anticipate issues, identify opportunities, and deliver practical, consistent guidance.
Coach managers through routine and moderately complex performance, feedback, and talent matters, including goal setting, performance documentation, corrective action, Performance Improvement Plans (PIP), talent development, and succession planning. Help managers apply expectations consistently and communicate clearly with employees.
Identify themes and trends across employee relations matters, exit feedback, engagement signals, workforce data, and other people metrics. Use data and qualitative insights to identify opportunities, develop recommendations, and communicate clear, compelling narratives to the Senior HRBPs and the broader People team to inform proactive action.
Contribute to the design, implementation, and continuous improvement of People programs, processes, policies, and manager resources. Support company and departmental diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility goals through inclusive and equitable People team practices.
Manage routine to moderately complex employee relations matters from intake through resolution, including conducting or supporting investigations, maintaining thorough and objective documentation, assessing potential risk, and recommending practical resolution options.
Advise and coordinate on timely employee lifecycle actions including job changes, promotions, transfers, reorganizations, leaves, accommodations, and terminations.
Support organizational change initiatives, including reorganizations, team changes, role changes, and other workforce transitions, in partnership with Senior HRBPs and business leaders. Help assess people impacts, identify risks and opportunities, and execute clear communication and transition plans.
Support organizational and team effectiveness initiatives by helping leaders understand workforce needs, organizational design considerations, and people-related implications of business decisions.
Support annual and recurring talent and people processes, including performance management, talent reviews, compensation planning, and promotions. Prepare managers for decision-making, promote consistency and fairness, and support effective communication of outcomes.
Guide managers in applying staffing, headcount, and compensation practices by coordinating with Compensation, Talent Acquisition, Finance, People Analytics, and other teams as needed.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Psychology, Business Administration, or a related field.
5+ years of progressive experience in Human Resources, including experience in an HR Generalist, HR Business Partner, or comparable role.
Ability to manage competing priorities, exercise sound judgment, and operate effectively in an environment with ambiguity and changing business needs.
Demonstrated willingness and courage to challenge senior leaders, push back constructively, and hold a firm stance on key people and organizational decisions.
Experience independently advising managers on employee relations, performance management, employee lifecycle processes, and conducting or supporting employee relations investigations.
Working knowledge of U.S. employment laws and HR compliance principles, including applying HR policies across multiple states.
Demonstrated business acumen and ability to understand how organizational goals, workforce needs, and business performance inform people decisions.
Demonstrated ability to build trusted relationships and establish rapport with managers, leaders, and employees at all levels of an organization.
Demonstrated discretion and ability to handle sensitive and confidential employee and business information with sound judgment.

Define what our metrics mean, rather than producing whatever is asked for

Fix the data underneath

Talent Partner - Referrals

At inspiring vet care, our people are at the heart of everything we do. As the UK’s number one vet care provider, we're trusted with the care of over 2 million animals, delivering our purpose of healthier animals and happier owners.

We’re looking for an accomplished recruiter to partner with our UK referral network, identifying and engaging exceptional veterinary professionals within one of the most specialised talent markets in the profession.

Referral recruitment requires a distinctly proactive and relationship-led approach. Success in this role will be driven by your ability to understand specialist talent markets in depth, identify and engage individuals who may not be actively considering their next career move, and build credible relationships over the longer term.

Combining headhunting, executive search principles, talent mapping and market intelligence, you’ll develop sustainable pipelines of specialist veterinary talent in multiple disciplines while partnering with senior clinical leaders to deliver both immediate and future workforce requirements.

This is a fully remote, home-based role, with travel required for meetings, veterinary congresses and industry events across the UK and Europe.

How You’ll Make a Difference

You’ll take ownership of recruitment across a portfolio of specialist referral vacancies, acting as a trusted Talent Partner to senior clinical and commercial leaders across our network.

Developing a detailed understanding of individual clinical disciplines and their respective talent markets will be central to your success. You’ll use this insight to shape recruitment strategies, advise on market conditions and provide an informed perspective on talent availability, compensation, attraction, relocation and international recruitment.

A significant focus of the role will be the proactive identification and engagement of specialist veterinary talent. Through systematic market mapping, targeted search and sustained relationship management, you’ll develop networks and pipelines that extend beyond current vacancies and strengthen our long-term ability to attract exceptional clinicians.

You’ll also:

Lead sophisticated headhunting and search strategies across specialist referral disciplines, using market mapping, professional networks and targeted sourcing to identify and engage high-calibre talent across the UK and internationally
Build and maintain meaningful long-term relationships with specialist clinicians, developing sustainable talent pipelines and communities across priority disciplines
Partner consultatively with senior clinical and hospital leaders, providing market intelligence and using evidence to influence recruitment strategy, compensation positioning, attraction approaches and realistic hiring expectations
Manage complex recruitment processes from initial engagement through to appointment, including assessment, candidate management, offer negotiation, relocation and visa sponsorship where appropriate
Represent inspiring vet care at specialist veterinary congresses, professional events and networking forums across the UK and Europe, strengthening our presence and relationships within the referral community
Use recruitment data, talent intelligence and pipeline analysis to continuously refine recruitment strategies, strengthen direct hiring capability and reduce reliance on external agencies

You Might Be a Great Fit If...

You bring significant experience of recruiting within specialist or talent-scarce markets, together with a strong track record in headhunting and/or executive search.

You are skilled at looking beyond the active candidate market: understanding where specialist talent sits, developing a comprehensive view of the market and establishing credible relationships with individuals whose career decisions may develop over an extended period.

Previous veterinary recruitment experience would be advantageous but is not essential. Of greater importance is your ability to apply sophisticated search methodology, develop specialist market expertise and operate as a credible recruitment partner to senior stakeholders.

You’ll bring:

Demonstrable expertise in headhunting, executive search, talent mapping and proactive direct sourcing within niche, specialist or difficult-to-source markets
Proven ability to identify and engage passive talent, establish credibility and develop long-term relationships through extended recruitment cycles
Strong stakeholder consulting capability, with the confidence and credibility to influence and constructively challenge senior leaders
Highly developed candidate management, assessment, negotiation and closing skills, with a focus on delivering an exceptional candidate experience
Strong commercial judgement and the ability to interpret market intelligence and recruitment data to shape effective talent strategies and prioritise activity
Excellent research, communication and relationship-building skills, combined with a proactive, resilient and highly collaborative approach
Experience within veterinary recruitment, healthcare or another specialist professional market would be advantageous, as would exposure to international recruitment, relocation and visa sponsorship.

How We’ll Support You

At inspiring vet care, we’re committed to supporting your ongoing development and wellbeing.

You’ll join an experienced Talent team and work closely with colleagues and clinical leaders who bring extensive knowledge of the veterinary profession and our referral network. We’ll support you in developing detailed knowledge of referral disciplines, specialist career pathways and the clinical communities you’ll recruit within.

You’ll have the autonomy to build and develop specialist talent networks, shape sourcing strategies and establish your own presence within the referral community, supported by opportunities to attend leading veterinary congresses and professional events across the UK and Europe.

You’ll also have the opportunity to take a genuinely long-term approach to talent acquisition. Alongside delivering against current recruitment priorities, you’ll build the relationships, market intelligence and talent pipelines that strengthen our ability to attract specialist clinicians well into the future.
